notes: Startup control - you can now switch logon entries on and off from inside Helix. Performance > Startup apps has a new "Runs at logon" column with a Disable/Enable button on every entry Helix is allowed to touch, covering all five places Windows looks for startup programs: your account's Run key, the two machine-wide ones, and both Startup folders. Disabling flips the same switch Task Manager uses instead of deleting anything, so it is fully reversible and survives an app rewriting its own startup entry. IT-managed agents show a "Managed" badge and are refused outright; machine-wide entries show "Needs admin". The counts on the page are re-read from Windows after every toggle rather than guessed, so they cannot drift from what is actually running. Also in this release: the action log now tells a deliberate refusal apart from a failure and shows the reason, and four more changes are recorded there - closing an app, sending a file to the Recycle Bin, creating a restore point, and running a troubleshooter fix.
